chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Beware of the thrice-divorced women, for they are women with husbands." The meaning in these narrations is also that if the divorce occurs during menstruation, or according to one of the cases we mentioned earlier where if it is so, no divorce takes effect, it is permissible that what is meant by this is the one whose divorce is conditional, for that is also among what does not take effect, according to what we previously stated regarding it, and what clarifies this meaning is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on thrice-divorced women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of a woman who has received three divorces, asserting that she is considered to have a husband (and thus not free to remarry the same man until she marries another). The text explains that this applies whether the divorce is effective immediately or conditional, and notes that the divorce may not take effect depending on specific conditions previously outlined.
